newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finmin warns of revenue shortfall in FY96/97.
newsitem.headline: Thai finmin warns of revenue shortfall in FY96/97.

text.p: Thailand's acting finance minister Chiyawat Wibulsawat said on Friday if the economy continues its current slow pace of growth, government revenues would not meet projections for the 1996/97 fiscal year.

"The budget year already began over a month ago," he said. "If the economy continues in this direction there is a high possibility that the government revenue (this year) would not meet earlier targets."
Thailand's fiscal year starts on October 1.
But Chaiyawat said he was confident the government would still post a fiscal surplus for the year because of the ministry's efforts to increase its revenue base and reduce unnecessary spending.
"With our tighter measures, the finance ministry is confident that the government will still have a fiscal surplus despite the lower revenues," he said.
Thailand follows a balanced budget policy when it approves budgets, but for the past eight years has posted a fiscal surplus.
Chaiyawat would not say how much of a surplus he expected the government to report for the year.
"As long as the government still has a fiscal surplus, it is still satisfactory," he said.
The Thai parliament has approved a record 984 billion baht ($39.36 billion) budget for the fiscal year.
Thailand's gross domestic product, which has grown an average of almost nine percent a year for the past decade, is projected by private economists to grow by less than seven percent this year.
